text:
Dave (Acme): Hey team — our org org_8732 hit a bunch of 429s right around local midnight last night. Dashboard still showed 0 credits and the app got throttled from ~00:05–00:18 PST. We expect monthly refill at midnight local. Can someone explain why we were still at 0? @Alice

Alice (Support): Hi Dave — sorry about that. Can you paste a short snippet of the client logs (request ids and timestamps) so we can correlate? Also which timezone is your account configured for (billing timezone)?

Dave (Acme): Account shows billing_tz=America/Los_Angeles. Logs:

```
2026-03-01T00:04:58-08:00 INFO request_id=req_aa1 status=429 attempt=1
2026-03-01T00:05:02-08:00 INFO request_id=req_aa2 status=429 attempt=1
2026-03-01T00:05:05-08:00 INFO request_id=req_aa1 status=429 attempt=2
2026-03-01T00:06:12-08:00 INFO request_id=req_aa3 status=200 tokens_used=312
```

Looks like a flood then some succeeded. We were expecting credits to top up at 00:00 local.

Alice (Support): Thanks — I'm pulling service-side logs. I'm also escalating to billing to confirm when the monthly refill job ran for org_8732. Ben, can you check the refill job and any downstream cache events?

Ben (Billing): Looking now. Quick summary: refill job runs for each tenant at their configured billing midnight, but the implementation does a conversion and schedules the DB update in UTC. For org_8732 (America/Los_Angeles), midnight local -> 07:00 UTC. Our logs show a successful DB update at 2026-03-01T07:00:01Z (refill applied).

Ben (Billing): Snippet from refill worker logs:

```
[2026-03-01T07:00:01Z] INFO tenant=org_8732 refill_job=monthly_refill status=applied new_balance=120000
[2026-03-01T07:00:01Z] INFO tenant=org_8732 publish=quota_invalidation event_id=evt_9f2
```

Alice (Support): That looks like the DB update succeeded. Carla, SRE — do we have evidence the cache invalidation event reached the cache layer? Dave reported UI still showed 0 at local midnight (00:05 PST).

Carla (SRE): Thanks. I pulled the cache/log stream. We saw the publish attempt (evt_9f2) but our event bus returned a transient error for the cache-invalidation message — it was retried and only delivered ~40 minutes later. Relevant log:

```
[2026-03-01T07:00:01Z] INFO publish evt_9f2 -> kinesis: ok
[2026-03-01T07:00:05Z] ERROR cache-invalidator: publish-to-redis failed: ConnectionReset
[2026-03-01T07:07:10Z] WARN cache-invalidator: retrying publish evt_9f2 (attempt=2)
[2026-03-01T07:41:03Z] INFO cache-invalidator: publish succeeded evt_9f2
[2026-03-01T07:41:03Z] INFO cache: invalidate tenant=org_8732
```

Carla (SRE): That means the DB had the new balance at 07:00Z (which is 00:00 PST), but the UI cache didn't get invalidated until ~07:41Z (~00:41 PST). The UI and edge caches continued to serve the old 0 balance until then.

Alice (Support): That explains why the dashboard showed 0. But Dave also reported 429s right at local midnight; if the DB had tokens at 07:00Z, why did requests get throttled?

Carla (SRE): Two contributing issues: 1) We observed a short burst of concurrent requests right before cache refresh where client retries + concurrency consumed the remaining pre-refill tokens. The refill logic writes a new total, but inflight requests are counted against the old bucket until the cache invalidation path is complete. 2) There was a bug in our throttling fallback: when cache read fails, some servers conservatively assume 0 available to avoid overspend, which triggers 429s while the DB update is in flight.

Carla (SRE): Example from token-allocator logs around 2026-03-01T07:00Z:

```
[2026-03-01T06:59:58Z] WARN token-allocator tenant=org_8732 cache_miss=true remaining_approx=0
[2026-03-01T07:00:00Z] INFO refill applied to DB tenant=org_8732 new_total=120000
[2026-03-01T07:00:03Z] INFO incoming_requests batch=concurrent(12) consumed=11800
[2026-03-01T07:00:04Z] WARN token-allocator returning=429 tenant=org_8732 reason=conservative_fallback
```

Carla (SRE): So a burst of concurrent requests plus the conservative fallback produced the observed 429s even though the DB had the refill. The cache invalidation being delayed made the window worse.

Dave (Acme): So to be clear: refill did happen at midnight local (07:00Z) but UI was stale and then our retries/concurrency consumed tokens? We didn't expect cache to matter for the refill itself.

Alice (Support): Correct summary. Refill applied to DB at the expected local midnight. UI visibility lag + conservative cache-failure behavior + a burst of retries caused the temporary throttling.

Ben (Billing): As a remediation for you: we've credited back 15k tokens to cover the burst consumption while we investigate — you should see that immediately in API responses (DB level) and in the console after caches refresh. I also flagged this org for manual review to ensure no other refill misfires this billing cycle.

Alice (Support): Long-term fixes we are doing:
- Carla's team will stop using the conservative 0 fallback when DB indicates a recent refill; instead we'll fallback to a short grace amount while cache is unreachable.
- We're adding a faster-path cache invalidation retry/backoff to avoid 40+ minute delays.
- We'll add a short preflight endpoint (/v1/credits/check) you can call before aggressive bursts to confirm visible balance (cheap, cached).

Carla (SRE): Patch has just been deployed to address the caching retry logic (deploy 1765432200). It changes the invalidation retry to exponential backoff + alarm on >5m delay.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: service/cache-invalidator fix/retry-exponential 1765432200 :white_check_mark:

Alice (Support): Practical mitigations for customers:
- Avoid synchronized retries at local midnight; jitter retry backoffs.
- Use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate spending from client retries.
- If you expect heavy synchronous traffic at reset boundary, pre-warm by calling the preflight endpoint once before the window.

Dave (Acme): Thanks — that helps a lot. One quick question: where is the canonical doc that states refill happens at tenant local midnight (and in what timezone it’s converted)? I'm going to share it with ops.

Alice (Support): We're updating docs but the current rule is: monthly refill is scheduled at tenant billing local midnight (we convert to UTC on the server). I'll send a doc link here once the page is updated. For now: midnight local -> server calculates UTC and runs the DB write at that converted UTC instant.

Ben (Billing): Also note DST caveats: on DST transitions the calculation is based on the stored tz region (e.g., America/Los_Angeles) so local midnight will follow DST shifts; the conversion is dynamic. We'll include a note in the docs.

Dave (Acme): Great. Appreciate the quick credit and the follow-ups. :thumbsup:

Alice (Support): You're welcome — I'll keep the thread open until the docs are live and the SRE patch is monitored for a few cycles. If anything else pops up ping me here.

Carla (SRE): Monitoring alerts set for cache-invalidation > 5m for tenant org_8732 for the next 72h.

Dave (Acme): Thanks, closing on my side but will re-open if we see more behavior.
